deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Controls how Terraform handles deletion of the resource. The ABANDON option can leave the target HTTP proxy running outside Terraform management, while DELETE permits removal of the resource. A policy should restrict deletion behaviour to approved values to reduce unmanaged infrastructure and accidental availability loss.

description.description: An optional description of this resource.
description.rationale: Provides optional descriptive metadata only and does not change access control, traffic routing, encryption, network exposure, or the security of the resource.

http_keep_alive_timeout_sec.description:
Specifies how long to keep a connection open, after completing a response,
while there is no matching traffic (in seconds). If an HTTP keepalive is
not specified, a default value will be used. For Global
external HTTP(S) load balancer, the default value is 610 seconds, the
minimum allowed value is 5 seconds and the maximum allowed value is 1200
seconds. For cross-region internal HTTP(S) load balancer, the default
value is 600 seconds, the minimum allowed value is 5 seconds, and the
maximum allowed value is 600 seconds. For Global external HTTP(S) load
balancer (classic), this option is not available publicly.
http_keep_alive_timeout_sec.rationale: Controls how long an idle HTTP connection remains open. The appropriate timeout depends on the workload and load-balancer design, so it is primarily a performance and availability setting and has no generic secure value that can be enforced.

name.description:
Name of the resource. Provided by the client when the resource is
created. The name must be 1-63 characters long, and comply with
RFC1035. Specifically, the name must be 1-63 characters long and match
the regular expression '[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?' which means the
first character must be a lowercase letter, and all following
characters must be a dash, lowercase letter, or digit, except the last
character, which cannot be a dash.
name.rationale: Only identifies the target HTTP proxy and does not change access control, traffic handling, network exposure, or the security of the resource or its data.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Identifies the Google Cloud project that owns the resource. The approved project is specific to each deployment and is normally controlled through provider configuration, IAM, and organisation policies, so a generic resource policy should not hardcode a project ID.

proxy_bind.description:
This field only applies when the forwarding rule that references
this target proxy has a loadBalancingScheme set to INTERNAL_SELF_MANAGED.
proxy_bind.rationale: Controls whether Envoy binds to the forwarding rule IP address and port to intercept inbound traffic for INTERNAL_SELF_MANAGED configurations. Enabling it changes network exposure and request handling, so a policy should require false unless gateway or middle-proxy behaviour has been explicitly approved.

url_map.description:
A reference to the UrlMap resource that defines the mapping from URL
to the BackendService.
url_map.rationale: References the URL map that defines routing to backend services. The correct URL map is application-specific, so a generic policy cannot safely restrict it to one identifier. Security controls should instead be applied to the configuration of the referenced URL map.
